skills.trigger: When evaluating a superior mediastinal mass on chest radiography to distinguish benign fatty tumors from other mediastinal pathologies.
steps: Inspect the PA view for a well-circumscribed, slightly lobulated soft-tissue density located in the superior mediastinum, typically projecting to one side (e.g., right paratracheal region).
Examine the lateral view specifically for increased soft-tissue density in the retrotracheal space, confirming the posterior mediastinal or prevertebral extension of the mass.
Differentiate from lymphadenopathy by noting the solitary, lobulated nature of the mass rather than bilateral or multifocal nodular enlargement.
Differentiate from duplication cysts by observing the lack of a perfectly round, smooth contour and absence of significant tracheal displacement, favoring a lipomatous origin.
